transcript: The Dolly Parton musical is officially coming to Broadway, and here's three reasons why I'm really excited for it now. Number one, I will admit I'm typically not a huge bio jukebox musical fan, but this one's actually doing something really interesting, where Dolly is also writing original music for the show. So in addition to her big hits like Jolene, 9 to 5, I will always love you, we are also getting original Dolly Parton music, which, of course, is exciting in its own right, but it's also going to give them a flexibility to tell the story that they actually want to tell without having to cram existing songs into moments where they may not fit, which is, like, the number one problem that I have with a lot of bio jukebox musicals. The second reason I'm excited is that this creative team is stacked. It's being directed by Bart Sher, who was behind all of the big Lincoln Center revivals. It's being choreographed by Mandy Moore from so you think you could Dance LA LA Land, the Errors Tour. And, of course, you have Dolly herself, who is no stranger to musical theater, having worked on the 9 to 5 musical, which I actually think is an incredibly underrated score. They did an out of town in Nashville last year, and I know that they've been making a ton of changes since, and I just have a lot of faith in this creative team to put together something That's really special. And the third and final reason is Dolly Parton herself. I just love everything she stands for, from her kindness and humility to her philanthropy work. I think she is such an inspiration, and I'm genuinely excited to just learn more about her life. And I think that a feel good Dolly Parton musical might just be exactly what the world needs right now.
classificationReason: Anticipation/announcement commentary about the Dolly Parton musical coming to Broadway; creator shares excitement about the creative team and concept but has not seen the show.
